title: Chazumba Mixtec - Wikipedia
text: Chazumba Mixtec is a Mixtec language of Puebla and Oaxaca, spoken in the towns of Santiago Chazumba, San Pedro y San Pablo Tequixtepec, Zapotitlán, Santa Gertrudis Cosoltepec, Petlalcingo (which it shares with Southern Puebla Mixtec), and Totoltepec de Guerrero.

title: Mixtec languages - Wikipedia
text: Through music or the way in which certain rituals are carried out, popular Mixtec literature has survived as it did for millennia: by means of oral transmission.

title: Chazumba Mixtec — Grokipedia
text: Chazumba Mixtec, as a Mixtec language, employs a tonal system, likely with multiple contrastive tones per syllable, essential for distinguishing words.

title: Mixtec, Chazumba Language (XTB) – L1 & L2 Speakers, Status ...
text: Chazumba Mixtec is an endangered indigenous language of Mexico. It belongs to the Otomanguean language family. The language is used as a first language by older adults only. It is not known to be taught in schools.

title: A Mixtec Sound Change Database - Journal of Open Humanities Data
text: We present an interlinked, expandable database of segmental sound changes among a large sample of Mixtec languages of Mexico. The database provides an up-to-date repository for scholars working on Mixtec and related languages.
